newsitem.title: USA: Greenpeace starts protest against altered soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace starts protest against altered soybeans.

text.p: Greenpeace activists on Monday demanded that genetically altered soybeans be taken off the market or separated from other soybeans, citing concerns about potential health problems.
"We are demanding that they be taken off the market or, at the very least, separated and labeled so that consumers know what they're getting," said Greenpeace spokeswoman Terri Johnson.

A press conference on board the MV Greenpeace, docked on the Mississippi River in downtown New Orleans, opened a week of planned activities in and around the Port of New Orleans, the nation's largest soybean export point.
The genetically altered "Roundup Ready" soybeans were developed by U.S. chemicals firm Monsanto to tolerate the company's "Roundup" weedkiller.

Bill Christison, vice president of the national Family Farmer Coalition, said, "By introducing seeds that are genetically engineered to survive heavy doses of their own toxic herbicide, Roundup, Monsanto is positioning themelves to control the production of the food and fiber (that) family farmers produce."

Johnson said the genetically altered soybeans were approved by the Food and Drug Administration after only 10 weeks of testing and without long-term studies of their potential impact on human health or the environment.
But authorities in the United States and Europe say the new Monsanto strain poses no danger to the human food chain.

Friday, Greenpeace activists ended a 24-hour blockade of a shipment of what they believed to be genetically-altered soybeans in the Belgian port of Antwerp after a court threatened to fine them $32,000 for every hour the protest continued.
